benchmark_consistency.common_basis: per-pass N2 conversion at the benchmark loop closure (3 beds, 698.15 K, 150 bar, SV 20 000 h^-1 normal, H2:N2 = 3, 0.5 mol % NH3 in the combined feed)
benchmark_consistency.status_expected: model-internal comparison of two literature figures; NOT external validation, and it does not close any open item of docs/28
benchmark_consistency.verdict_rule: decided BEFORE the run, from the opened sources only: the pair counts as mutually consistent if (i) the per-pass conversion implied by the outlet figure lies inside the union of the opened per-pass bands (15-20 % Humphreys, 15-25 % RSC EES -> 15-25 %) and (ii) the local slope of the rate->outcome curve predicts the gap to within 50 % (|predicted/actual - 1| <= 0.5), i.e. the activity factor is a consequence of the near-pinch sensitivity rather than an independent contradiction in the data
benchmark_consistency.note: matching the outlet figure needs a per-pass conversion of 22.30 %, which is outside the narrow opened band (15-20 %) and inside the wider opened band (15-25 %); the 0.373-decade activity difference between the two objectives is worth 5.52 pp of per-pass conversion at this operating point, and the actual gap is 4.80 pp (linearised estimate is off by 15 % because the curve is concave near the pinch). So the two sources disagree by a few points of conversion, not by a factor of 2.36 in activity: the large factor is the model's own near-pinch sensitivity, and a corridor (docs/32) is the only honest way to report the design.
benchmark_consistency.status: [ПОДТВЕРЖДЕНО] both figures reduced to one basis, tolerance taken from the opened bands

layout_scan.question: which multi-bed / cold-shot layout keeps T_peak at or below the assumed catalyst ceiling while preserving conversion
layout_scan.finding: the ceiling is never the limiting factor on its own: every layout can be kept at or below 803 K by lowering the common bed inlet (628-666 K found here), and the per-pass conversion stays 14.8-23.1% at unchanged catalyst volume. Splitting the same volume over more beds RAISES the allowable inlet temperature (628 K at 2 beds -> 666 K at 5 beds) because the first bed then carries a smaller share of the total volume. The real trade-off is with the outlet ammonia concentration: cold shot pulls per-pass conversion into the opened 15-20% band but dilutes the product gas, so outlet NH3 falls from 13.21 mol% (5 beds, no quench) to 10.61 mol% (3 beds, 15% quench) - which the opened benchmark does not measure, because it quotes per-pass conversion at a plant recycle ratio we do not know.
layout_scan.note: cold shot is modelled as fresh feed injected between beds and the mixture then tempered to the common bed-inlet temperature, i.e. the quench is assumed sufficient and the interbed exchanger duty is what remains after it. The reported duty is the sensible-enthalpy drop of the bed effluent to the next inlet at the SAME composition: the enthalpy credit of mixing in unpreheated fresh feed is not netted against it, so layouts with a large quench are counted conservatively (duty overstated by up to the cold-feed preheat share). Converter internals (distributor, quench control, bed hydraulics) are NOT modelled
layout_scan.status: [ЧАСТИЧНО] layout comparison uses the calibrated activity and the assumed bed ceiling; no vendor layout data (docs/28)
